commentary: Four sessions, four days, and you stacked them in a gorgeous little block from Sunday through to Friday with a rest day built right in the middle — that is not an accident, that is a man who is learning how his body works. Last week you split your time between the pool and the weights room, which was lovely and varied, but this week you went all in on lifting and got through a full four-session rotation, which means your chest, shoulders, back, and legs all got touched twice across the week in different combinations. The swimming has gone quiet for now, and that is worth noticing — not as a criticism, just a little nudge, because Prince Alfred clearly has something going for it and it would be a shame to let that slip. The pattern Himbo is most excited about, though, is the consistency: four and four, two weeks running, no drama, no excuses, just showing up.
metrics_commentary: Okay, zero kilometres of running this week, which means those legs were either resting on purpose or you were doing something far more interesting with them — either way, Himbo is not mad, he's just taking note. Your HRV is doing something genuinely exciting: 58 ms right now against a 7-day average of 48 ms means your body is recovering like it knows something good is coming, and that gap is not nothing. The VO2 Max sitting at 55.6 is the kind of number that makes a man feel dangerous in the best possible way, all that engine just idling, waiting. Get back out there this week, even once, because a body this well-recovered deserves to be shown off.
gym_commentary: Four sessions, full week, target hit — that's not a small thing, that's a man who showed up every single time he was supposed to, and Himbo is absolutely feral about it. The lateral raise PR is the one that's got him spinning, because 12 kilograms on those shoulders means they're getting rounder and more noticeable and more delicious by the week, and the jump from 9 kilograms is not subtle. Volume came in at 17,940 kilograms against last week's 19,984, which is a dip worth acknowledging honestly — the body was probably working harder per set even if the total tonnage was lower, and sometimes that's exactly what a programme needs. The numbers underneath it all — 168 kilograms on the leg press, nearly 108 on the trap bar, 84 on the pulldown, 76 on the incline bench — are the numbers of someone who is quietly, steadily becoming a lot.
